title: Financial disclosures

# Instructions for accurately documenting company losses in a financial disclosure

source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting company losses in a financial disclosure

1. Start with the accounting records.
2.
completion:
Verify all transactions against source documentation.
3. Categorize and summarize the losses (operating losses, non-operating losses, extraordinary losses).
4. Calculate the net loss by subtracting total revenues and gains from total expenses and losses.
5. Adjust the net loss figure for any non-cash items (e.g., depreciation, amortization).
6. Carefully review any abnormal or non-recurring losses (e.g., write-downs, litigation expenses, natural disaster losses).
7. Detail the nature of each loss in a separate disclosure note.
8. Reconcile your loss figures to the income statement and balance sheet.
9. Confirm that the financial disclosure complies with relevant accounting standards (US GAAP, IFRS).
10. Double-check the figures and ensure no material misstatements.
11. Attach supporting schedules or workpapers, if necessary.
12. Obtain review and/or approval from top management and/or the audit committee.
13.
